observation_scheduler.observation_scheduler_policy: solve_to returns exactly len(save_times) frames; frame i is the state at save_times[i]; the gap between two requested observations is covered by ceil(gap/dt_max) equal sub-steps of size gap/ceil(gap/dt_max) so that the integrator lands exactly on the requested time; dt_max is the solver's own stability bound evaluated on the current state.

time_stepping_policy.observation_scheduler_policy: solve_to returns exactly len(save_times) frames; frame i is the state at save_times[i]; the gap between two requested observations is covered by ceil(gap/dt_max) equal sub-steps of size gap/ceil(gap/dt_max) so that the integrator lands exactly on the requested time; dt_max is the solver's own stability bound evaluated on the current state.
time_stepping_policy.internal_step_rule: min(stable_internal_dt, next_observation_gap), sub-divided into ceil(gap/stable_internal_dt) equal steps so the integrator lands exactly on the observation
time_stepping_policy.stability_bound: min(cfl*dx/alpha, dx^2/(alpha*dx + 2*nu)) with alpha = max|u|; the second term is the combined advection-diffusion von Neumann bound and is not the minimum of the separate bounds

dataset_manifest.split_seed_policy: train/val initial conditions are spawned from `split_seed`; the test split is spawned from its own `test_split_seed` so that the final test set is independent of the development set

wsl_filesystem.scope: the WSL root filesystem (a virtual disk). Its free space is NOT the physical free space of the Windows volume that backs it; the physical figure is reported separately.

preflight.disk_scope_note: the WSL filesystem figure is the size of the distribution's virtual disk; the physical free space of the Windows volume that backs it is reported separately under host.windows_physical_disk
preflight.lock_scope_note: the project job lock excludes cooperating PDELab jobs only. It is not a system-wide scheduler and it does not protect the GPU against unrelated software.

determinism.note: GPU reductions and FFT kernels are not bitwise deterministic; a seeded run is reproducible in configuration, initialisation and data order, but not necessarily in the last floating-point digits
